claims.text: Comprehensive evaluation of AI-related risks requires assessing both model-specific bottom-up risks and organizational governance top-down risks.
An end-to-end AI risk management kernel can be structured into five implementation steps: Identify, Collect, Assess, Comply, and Monitor.
Scaling an AI risk auditing tool requires a role-based approach covering different roles involved in complex AI system development.
Integrating an AI auditing tool within existing governance infrastructure reduces compliance barriers for regulatory standards like the EU AI Act and ISO 42001:2023.

evidence.description: To attain a comprehensive understanding of all AI-related risks, it is essential to evaluate both model-specific risks and those associated with the organizational and governance setups.
Our end-to-end (from identification to monitoring) risk management kernel follows these implementation steps: - Identify - Collect - Assess - Comply - Monitor.

We demonstrate that scaling of such a risk auditing tool requires fundamental aspects. Those aspects include for instance a role-based approach, covering different roles in the development of complex AI systems.

This integration is essential to reduce the barriers for companies to comply with current regulatory requirements, such as the EU AI Act [European Parliament and the Council of the EU, 2024], and established standards like ISO 42001:2023.

methodologies.name: AI Governance Risk Management Kernel
methodologies.description: A five-step end-to-end auditing framework (Identify, Collect, Assess, Comply, Monitor) that maps traditional risk management practices to AI systems and existing enterprise governance infrastructure.
